title: No integer equivalent form for the ⟨2,4,5;32⟩ and ⟨3,3,6;40⟩ ℤ[1/2] matrix multiplication schemes
statement: Let K be a field of characteristic 0. For a scheme (a_r, b_r, c_r), r = 1..R, for the format ⟨n,m,p⟩ (a_r: n×m, b_r: m×p, c_r: p×n, satisfying the Brent equations), call (λ_r U a_r V⁻¹, μ_r V b_r W⁻¹, (λ_r μ_r)⁻¹ W c_r U⁻¹) with U ∈ GL_n(K), V ∈ GL_m(K), W ∈ GL_p(K), λ_r, μ_r ∈ K^×, possibly followed by a reordering of the terms, an equivalent form. Then neither the ⟨2,4,5;32⟩ scheme of AlphaEvolve (2025) nor the ⟨3,3,6;40⟩ scheme of Smirnov (2013), both with coefficients in ℤ[1/2] (as in the pinned files named in the README), has an equivalent form all of whose coefficients are integers. Certificates (the type of Moran–Schwartz–Yuan, Proposition 3), with term matrices M_j = a_j b_j c_j: tr(M_1) = 3/2 for ⟨3,3,6;40⟩ and tr(M_2 M_5) = 1/2 for ⟨2,4,5;32⟩. The action conjugates every M_j by U (term scalings cancel), so these traces are invariant, and they would be integers for an integer form.

sources.authors: Moran, Y.; Schwartz, O.; Yuan, S.
sources.title: Complex to Rational Fast Matrix Multiplication
sources.note: Proposition 3 and §3.2 (Integer algorithms): the result for Smirnov's ⟨3,3,6,40⟩ (single trace not in ℤ) and for a ⟨2,4,5,32⟩ algorithm over ℤ[1/2] (trace of a product of two term matrices not in ℤ), which they attribute to Hopcroft and Kerr (1971). The note uses certificates of this type.
